name: Cowboy State Eats: Wyoming
subtitle: Saloons, Steaks & Small Towns
description:
Wyoming's restaurants, from Hartville's frontier saloon to a scratch-made soda in Chugwater.

Cowboy State Eats is a free guide to eating in Wyoming: 9 historic saloons, 5 steakhouses and cookouts, 10 small-town cafés, 6 soda fountains and ice cream stops, 7 farm-to-table kitchens, 4 pizzerias and 7 historic hotel dining rooms we checked by hand, plus 1,422 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 116 towns, from Cheyenne and Casper to Jackson and Cody. No account, no ads.

WYOMING GUIDES
• Historic Saloons: frontier bars, from Hartville's carved back bar to Jackson's saddle stools.
• Steakhouses & Cookouts: steak, wild game and a Wind River cookout.
• Small-Town Cafés: breakfast cafés, diners and bakeries in small towns.
• Soda Fountains & Ice Cream: Chugwater to Jackson.
• Farm to Table: kitchens cooking from Wyoming ranches and farms.
• Pizza and Historic Hotel Dining.
• Oldest Places: 9 restaurants open since 1960 or earlier.
• James Beard Honors: 5 honored Wyoming restaurants.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "saloon", "bison jackson", "soda fountain".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a dated 2025 or 2026 Travel Wyoming article or Travel Wyoming's own listing. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by the reliability rule tested in the states that publish official restaurant lists. Wyoming posts no grades and publishes no inspection results as data, so each place links the Department of Agriculture's inspection reports page. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Cowboy State Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of Wyoming, the Wyoming Department of Agriculture or Travel Wyoming), or with the James Beard Foundation. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Cowboy State Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Wyoming (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: historic saloons, steakhouses and cookouts, small-town cafés, soda fountains, farm-to-table kitchens, pizza and historic hotel dining, 45 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the James Beard honorees. It also lists 1,422 restaurants, cafés and bars in 116 towns from open map data. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Historic Saloons (or Steakhouses & Cookouts, Small-Town Cafés, Soda Fountains & Ice Cream, Farm to Table, Pizza, Historic Hotel Dining, James Beard Honors, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down, a link opens the Wyoming Department of Agriculture's inspection reports page in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("saloon", "bison jackson", "soda fountain").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Wyoming (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Wyoming, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "Cowboy State Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Cowboy State Eats: Wyoming".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Cowboy State Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites, local news and Travel Wyoming's listings.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/wyoming-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Wyoming; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. The app shows no inspection results and computes no grades. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the James Beard Foundation.
